summary: Event-Driven Ansible activations run ansible-rulebook against event sources or event streams, using EDA hybrid nodes, the gateway, the WebSocket server and the database; load depends on event rate and rule complexity. Auditing each event through the WebSocket server to the database is costly; Skip audit events removes this while rules still fire, with fire counts updated every 300 seconds.
questions: How do I reduce Event-Driven Ansible database load?
What does Skip audit events do in an activation?
Why are rule fire counts delayed in EDA?

answer_card.title: Skip audit events for busy EDA activations
answer_card.answer_md:
Each event an activation processes is sent to the WebSocket server and written to the database for auditing (on by default), which can cause performance problems at high event rates.

Select **Skip audit events** on the activation to remove that workload. Rules still fire and launch jobs, but the fire count in the UI and API updates periodically (default every 300 seconds) instead of immediately.
